Job Description:
About VaultN 

VaultN is building the games industry’s fastest-growing digital distribution platform, powering many of the world’s leading publishers. Our commercial infrastructure connects distribution, payments, marketing, and data- unifying a long-fragmented industry through technology, automation, and intelligence. 

Backed by global investors including Sony Innovation Fund and London Venture Partners, VaultN is at the stage where the people who join today will shape how games are sold and distributed worldwide for years to come.

The next chapter needs real financial strength. You are joining not to maintain what exists, but to design and build the financial processes,structures and insights that will support what comes next.

Role Overview

In this role, you will own a variety of testing methods; manual, exploratory, and automated with a strong emphasis on automation, which is the team's biggest current gap. This is a foundational role: you'll be building QA automation practices and standards from the ground up, not maintaining an already-mature setup. Working closely with cross-functional teams in an Agile environment, you will design and maintain test automation frameworks, integrate testing into CI/CD pipelines, and help extend the capabilities of ARTI, our AI testing agent. AI-driven ideas for how we test and assure quality are welcome and encouraged.
You'll work alongside existing QA expertise on the team in manual and exploratory testing, helping build the standards, tooling, and automation coverage needed for VaultN to release frequently and confidently.

Key Responsibilities:

Strong programming skills in languages used for test automation (Java, JavaScript/TypeScript). 
Min. 5 years of solid experience in software manual testing and test automation. 
Hands-on experience creating web application tests using Selenium, Cucumber, TestNG/JUnit, and API testing using Rest-Assured, etc. 
Recent hands-on experience with test automation tools Cypress (JS) or Playwright (JS/TS). 
Knowledge of task tracking, error reporting, and project management tools; not limited to Jira, Jira Xray, TestRail. 
Strong API testing experience using tools such as Postman. 
Proficiency with Git and GitHub or similar version control systems. 
Basic knowledge of relational databases and SQL skills. 
Good understanding of QA testing methodologies, test planning, system dependencies, and product integration phases. 
Analytical thinking, problem-solving, and strong communication skills. 
Ability to work in a team, responsible, and successful in human relationships. 
Detail-oriented, careful, and analytical thinking. 
Ability to maintain documentation discipline.
English is a must for daily scrum meetings, reporting, and documentation. 

QA Key Objectives:

Align the QA process with the team's 2-week sprint cadence within our Agile methodology. 
Build an AI-driven, scalable quality engineering capability that enables VaultN to release frequently and confidently without QA becoming a bottleneck. 
Design, develop, and maintain the test automation framework, and validate execution reliability. 
Write and execute test cases both manually and on the CI/CD pipeline, based on current and past sprint work completed by the development and QA teams. 
Develop and execute non-functional tests. 
Build and maintain test automation pipelines and infrastructure. 
Track errors occurring during tests through test management tools. 
Identify defects, report them clearly in the relevant tools, and track them to completion. 
Bring and build automation standards for the development team. 
Teach and expand ARTI's testing capabilities, growing what it can validate autonomously over time. 
Partner with the team's existing manual/exploratory QA expertise to raise overall automation maturity.

Will be a plus:
Experience in performance testing using JMeter, K6, or similar. 
Experience with CI/CD (e.g. Jenkins, AWS, Azure DevOps) general DevOps knowledge. 
Prior use of DevOps/DORA metrics as a foundation for driving QA standards. 
ISTQB certification. 
Bachelor's/Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline (nice to have, not required). 
Domain knowledge of high-transaction infrastructure and/or the gaming industry (not mandatory, but a strong plus).

Why Join VaultN

This role sits at the heart of how quality scales as VaultN grows. The automation, standards, and AI-driven testing capability you build will directly shape how confidently and how quickly we can release, how much developers can trust the pipeline, and how far ARTI can take on testing work on its own.
You'll join a team where ownership is real, processes are still being built, and a good idea can become how we work next week. We're small enough that what you build will matter, and big enough that the testing challenge is genuinely interesting to solve.

What We Offer

Salary range €5,400 – €6,500 gross per month. Where you land in the range depends on the experience you bring and how directly applicable it is, in other words, how quickly you can be effective in the role.
SARs (Stock Appreciation Rights) participation as an early team member, your upside grows with the business you help build.
Hybrid working setup, flexibility on location, with regular time at our Amsterdam office. Working from office 4 days in a week. After first 3 months assign 2 extra work from home day per month.
Room to grow. As VaultN scales, this role can develop towards broader QA or quality engineering leadership.

How to Apply

Send your CV and a short note on a testing or automation problem you've solved — a framework you built, a flaky test suite you stabilized, a pipeline you automated — to [hr@vaultn.com].
Our process: an intro call, a structured interview with our tech team, an invitation to the office for a final meeting with our CEO, CTO, and COO, and a practical exercise focused on AI-driven testing. We aim to come back to you within 48 hours of each step.

Job Description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About This Team And Role

We are looking for an experienced and versatile software engineer to work on the tools and systems that support Firefox engineering.

This is a broad software engineering role spanning internal engineering systems, developer tooling, workflow automation, and the infrastructure required to operate them. We are looking for an engineer with strong software development skills and meaningful experience deploying and operating production systems.

Our Cloud Engineering teams provide shared platforms and foundational services, while engineering teams own the applications and services they run on them. A key part of this role is helping teams succeed in that model by solving difficult operational problems, establishing standards and patterns, and building tooling and automation that makes systems easier to operate. You will also contribute directly to the software, tools, and systems that support Firefox engineering.

You will work across projects and technical domains, joining teams or existing efforts when needed and independently taking on problems that require focused ownership.

What You'll Do

Design, build, deploy, and operate software and systems supporting Firefox engineering.
Contribute to developer tooling, CI/CD, workflow automation, and AI-assisted development tools.
Own complex technical problems end-to-end across software, cloud, and operational layers, improving reliability, performance, observability, and cost efficiency.

Use telemetry, metrics, and data analysis to investigate problems and guide engineering decisions.
Contribute to architecture and technical strategy, identifying recurring problems and solutions that can be applied across teams.

What you'll bring:

Strong software engineering skills and substantial hands-on experience deploying and operating production systems are core requirements for this role. We do not expect you to be an expert in every technology or domain listed below.

Strong programming skills in languages such as Python or JavaScript/TypeScript. Experience with C++ or Rust is useful.
Experience building and deploying and operating production systems in cloud environments, including utilizing infrastructure as code such as Terraform.
Experience across several areas such as CI/CD, containers and orchestration, networking, databases, observability, or developer tooling.
Experience using data, telemetry, and metrics to investigate technical problems and make decisions.
Familiarity with modern AI-assisted development tools and an understanding of their capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use.

How you work:

You are comfortable jumping into unfamiliar systems and getting them into a sustainable state.
You enjoy moving across projects and technical domains, taking ownership of problems and looking for patterns that make the next one easier to solve.
You work effectively across disciplines and can translate between software, infrastructure, and operational concerns.
You combine hands-on engineering with systems thinking and longer-term technical judgment.
You communicate openly, consistently, and respectfully, and enjoy teaching and helping others build skills in unfamiliar technical areas.

Job Description:
As a Senior Engineer in Global Workplace Services, you will be a technical authority and hands-on platform engineer for Microsoft 365, AI and automation capabilities used across ING. You will design, operate and continuously improve the generic Microsoft 365 platform, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, connectors, consumption-based services and the automation capabilities that support our workplace services.

You will build secure and scalable platform solutions, automation pipelines and straight-through processes that reduce manual work and improve operational quality. You will also contribute to the operation and development of Exchange and Messaging capabilities where your experience and interests align.

In this role, you combine deep engineering expertise with platform governance, secure AI adoption, operational resilience, cost control, compliance and stakeholder collaboration.

Team

The purpose of Global Workplace Services is to provide ING colleagues with a Digital Workplace in which they can collaborate frictionlessly in a hybrid world. Global Workplace Services enables colleagues worldwide to do their jobs as effectively as possible, using modern digital tools that are secure, up to date and user-friendly.

The Workplace department maximizes value for employees by leveraging the Microsoft Cloud Platform across collaboration, productivity, communication, automation and employee-experience services. Workplace owns and manages Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Platform and related platform capabilities, including the governance, automation and operational controls needed to operate these services safely at enterprise scale.

M365 Automation, Platform & Messaging Chapter provides secure, resilient and scalable Microsoft 365 workplace platform capabilities. The chapter manages generic Microsoft 365 platform services; Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio; automation for self-service, provisioning, reporting and platform operations; and Messaging services such as Exchange, fax and compliance archiving.

The chapter develops reusable automation libraries and engineering patterns, manages integrations and connectors, improves platform observability and resolves complex technical and security incidents.

Roles And Responsibilities

As a Senior Engineer in Global Workplace Services, you will act as a subject-matter expert and hands-on engineer across Microsoft 365 platform capabilities, AI and automation. You will be responsible for designing, implementing and operating secure, reliable and scalable services that support employee productivity and enable controlled innovation across ING.

Microsoft 365 Platform Engineering


Design, configure, operate and continuously improve generic Microsoft 365 tenant and platform capabilities.
Translate business, security, risk and compliance requirements into scalable configurations, engineering standards and platform guardrails.
Develop and maintain configuration standards, access models, operational procedures and lifecycle processes for Microsoft 365 services.
Monitor Microsoft service health, product changes and platform dependencies, and assess their potential impact on ING.
Contribute to technical designs, architecture reviews, platform roadmaps and engineering decisions.
Use automation and configuration control to improve the consistency, traceability and maintainability of Microsoft 365 services.
Provide technical leadership during complex incidents, investigations, platform changes and service escalations.
Work with engineers across other Workplace chapters to improve shared platform capabilities and reduce duplication.



AI, Copilot and Agent Platform Engineering


Design, configure, operate and continuously improve Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio platform capabilities.
Engineer and support enterprise-grade agents, agentic workflows and integrations with Microsoft 365 and other enterprise systems.
Design integration patterns using Microsoft Graph, APIs, Power Platform connectors, custom connectors and other approved interoperability mechanisms.
Configure and manage Copilot Studio and Power Platform environments, including access models, environment strategy, data policies and application-lifecycle controls.
Establish reusable engineering patterns for agent development, testing, deployment, monitoring and support.
Support the controlled use of Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors and Power Platform connectors, including technical assessment, access control and lifecycle management.
Engineer and operate Pay-As-You-Go and other consumption-based platform capabilities, including billing policies, access groups, usage monitoring and cost controls.
Implement monitoring, evaluation and feedback mechanisms for AI services and agents, covering service health, usage, quality, failures, cost and operational risk.
Help ensure that AI solutions remain secure, observable, auditable and aligned with ING’s responsible-AI, data-protection and regulatory requirements.
Apply human oversight, least privilege and secure-by-design principles when AI is connected to workflows, enterprise data or business processes.



Power Platform and Connector Governance


Operate and improve Power Platform capabilities used for enterprise automation and AI integration.
Design and maintain environment strategies, Managed Environments, access models and application-lifecycle processes.
Implement Data Loss Prevention policies and connector controls that enable appropriate innovation while protecting enterprise data.
Assess standard, premium and custom connectors for security, authentication, authorization, data handling, supportability and operational ownership.
Support makers and engineering teams with approved patterns for developing, testing and promoting solutions through development, acceptance and production environments.
Automate environment provisioning, policy assignment, deployment and monitoring where appropriate.
Contribute to an operating model in which solutions have clear ownership, lifecycle management, support arrangements and production controls.



Automation and Straight-Through Processing


Design, develop and operate automation solutions for self-service requests, user and service provisioning, platform administration, reporting and operational controls.
Build straight-through processes that take requests from intake through validation, approval, implementation, evidence capture and completion with minimal manual intervention.
Develop reusable automation components, services, scripts and runbooks using technologies such as PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, REST APIs, Power Automate and Azure services.
Design and maintain Azure DevOps pipelines for build, test, deployment and configuration-management activities.
Apply Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery practices to platform automation and agent solutions.
Integrate automation with systems such as ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Entra ID and other enterprise platforms.
Implement appropriate exception handling, logging, approvals, segregation of duties and rollback capabilities.
Develop desired-state monitoring and configuration-control capabilities to identify drift and improve platform stability.
Replace repetitive manual processes with secure, auditable and reusable automation wherever this delivers measurable value.
Produce operational reporting and telemetry that improve insight into service health, provisioning, usage, costs, risks and control effectiveness.



Messaging and Exchange Engineering

Experience with Exchange and Messaging technologies is a strong advantage for this position. Depending on your expertise, you may also:


Design, configure and operate Exchange Online and related Messaging capabilities.
Engineer solutions involving mail flow, transport rules, connectors, mailboxes, distribution capabilities and hybrid or cross-tenant dependencies.
Support compliance archiving, retention, eDiscovery and regulatory Messaging requirements in collaboration with security and compliance specialists.
Automate Messaging administration, provisioning, reporting and configuration validation.
Monitor service health, message flow, security signals, capacity and platform changes.
Lead troubleshooting for complex Messaging incidents and integration issues.
Contribute to the modernization of legacy Messaging integrations and authentication patterns.



Operational Excellence, Security and Risk


Apply strong engineering practices, including secure coding, peer review, automated testing, configuration control, documentation, monitoring and structured problem management.
Ensure platform changes and automation are reproducible, traceable, auditable and supported by appropriate evidence.
Identify and mitigate risks related to Microsoft 365, AI, automation, integrations, connectors and Messaging services.
Contribute to cyber-resilience, business-continuity, audit, privacy, sourcing and compliance activities.

You will work with browser automation tools, including existing Puppeteer workflows that are being phased out, and integrations with third-party automation providers.
